note: MAPPING (paper_order): nothing in the study ties PHQ_1..PHQ_9 to text. The OSF deposit (the node's only file; no child components) is a CSV with bare headers and no label row, and the paper (preprint section 2.2.2) names and describes the PHQ-9 but never prints an item. data/smpi_lorenzoluaces.py keeps the source names PHQ_1..PHQ_9 unchanged (dict by name, no positional step), so the alignment rests on the official PHQ-9 form's printed numbering 1-9 matching the column suffix; 'paper_order' is recorded, as for the sibling smpi_lorenzoluaces_2020_gad7 (batch_176), because the order is the instrument form's, not this paper's. STEP 5b (verify_smpi_lorenzoluaces_2020_phq9.R, PARTIAL, VERDICT: PASS): live PHQ_i equals deposit PHQ_i in 4383/4383 cells incl. NA pattern. Using the same 487 respondents' SMPI answers (item wording printed in the paper's Table 1) and SHAPS: PHQ_4 is the strongest correlate of SMPI A1 'very low energy' (0.333 vs 0.154-0.287); PHQ_8 of A6 'distinctly physically slowed' (0.389 vs 0.082-0.200); PHQ_7 of A7 'concentration is distinctly affected' (0.383 vs 0.143-0.254); PHQ_5 of B6 'food cravings and/or increased appetite' (0.335 vs 0.050-0.181); PHQ_1 of A4 'completely lose interest' (0.353 vs 0.141-0.244) and the most negative correlate of the SHAPS total (-0.535 vs -0.250 to -0.484). PHQ_9 is the least endorsed item other than the pinned psychomotor item (mean 0.487, 70.6% at 0; next 1.039). Of the remaining {PHQ_2, PHQ_3, PHQ_6}, only PHQ_3 has the energy item PHQ_4 as its strongest within-PHQ partner (r=0.59; PHQ_2 and PHQ_6 pair with each other at r=0.78), the sleep-fatigue somatic pairing. NOT ESTABLISHED: PHQ_2 vs PHQ_6 are not distinguished from each other; the SMPI legs assume SMPIa_i/SMPIb_i follow Table 1 order; the PHQ_9 and PHQ_3 legs are distributional/structural rather than content twins. OPTIONS: shipped the PHQ-9 form's anchors 0 Not at all / 1 Several days / 2 More than half the days / 3 Nearly every day. Direction: raw item sum equals the deposit's PHQ column, reproduces the paper's M 9.80 (SD 6.40) for this subsample (complete n=481) and its PHQ-9>=10 count among completed-SMPI cases (216 vs paper 216), and correlates 0.727 with the GAD-7 total (paper r=.73; GAD direction established in batch_176); items 8 and 9 sit 81%/71% at 0, consistent only with 0 = lowest frequency. CAVEAT: the paper's Methods describe the response scale as 0-3 'with 0 being "none of the days" and 3 being "all the days"' (the same sentence it uses for the GAD-7), which is not the PHQ-9 form's anchor wording; no source shows the administered labels (the deposit has none, the preprint prints no questionnaire), so the canonical anchors are shipped and the discrepancy is disclosed in public_note. The paper gives no middle-anchor wording. TEXT: items and instructions verbatim from PHQ-9_English.pdf with leading item numbers stripped and line wraps joined; em dashes in items 6 and 8, item 8's internal '? Or the opposite', and item 9 without a comma after 'dead' kept as printed on that form (older PHQ-9 printings differ slightly in punctuation; which printing the study used is unknown). The form's paper-only line '(Use "✔" to indicate your answer)' is omitted from instructions because the study was an online MTurk survey, and the form's unnumbered functional-difficulty question is not in this table and not shipped. LANGUAGE: English (US MTurk sample), so no language/_translated columns. RIGHTS: register row 'PHQ and GAD screener family (PHQ-2/9, GAD-2/7)' verdict ship, applied not re-derived; re-confirmed at source: the fetched PDF footer reads 'Developed by Drs. Robert L. Spitzer, Janet B.W. Williams, Kurt Kroenke and colleagues, with an educational grant from Pfizer Inc. No permission required to reproduce, translate, display or distribute.' STEP 3b: clean -- 9 items, resp 0-3, per-item n 485-487 each with all 4 levels (irw_table_sets), deposit total range 0-27, matching the PHQ-9 and not the GAD-7 (7), SHAPS (14) or SMPI (24, 1-5) in the same file. RESPONSE-DATA OBSERVATIONS (not item-text issues): the paper reports the PHQ-9 for n=1503 full-sample completers (mean 5.13), but the deposit and so the IRW table hold only the 487 routed to the SMPI (mean 9.80); six cells are missing (PHQ_2 n=485, PHQ_3-PHQ_6 n=486). The psychomotor item PHQ_8 (mean 0.279) is less endorsed than the suicidal-ideation item PHQ_9 (0.487), the reverse of the usual community-sample ordering; its SMPI A6 twin (0.389 vs <=0.200) pins it regardless.
public_note: The PHQ-9 item and response-option wording here is the published instrument's; the study's paper describes its 0-3 scale endpoints as "none of the days" and "all the days" rather than the PHQ-9's "Not at all" and "Nearly every day", and no source shows the labels respondents actually saw

note: PASS WITH CAVEATS (batch_177). 40 rows, 10 items x resp 1-4; validate_items.R --table-sets passes both sets; per-item n a uniform 1238 (server-side aggregates). STEP 3b: clean. Live shape is 10 items on 1-4; the deposit's RSES1..RSES10 columns sit beside SLWAI1..22 and MPATS1..16, and the paper describes RSES as '10 four-point Likert items'. CODE DERIVATION: pattern 1 -- item IS the source column name (script melts RSES1..RSES10 straight off the xlsx header). But that header carries no text at any level (bare codes, no comments, no second sheet), so the exemption buys nothing and none is claimed. SOURCES CHECKED FOR ITEM TEXT: all seven supplements. s001/s002 are SEM figure TIFFs, s003-s006 are TIFF images of Tables 1-4 (demographics, correlations, regression, path coefficients -- read directly, no item wording), s007 is the xlsx with bare codes. The paper body prints no item list and no anchor labels. The article HTML has zero CJK characters; the xlsx has CJK only in Chinese-locale Excel furniture (font 宋体, style names such as 常规, sheet-type label 工作表 in styles.xml/theme1.xml/app.xml), none in sharedStrings or cell content. So text_source=translated_substitute. LANGUAGE: recorded as Chinese, but the paper does NOT state the questionnaire language outright: participants were mainland Chinese medical students (China Medical University, Shenyang) recruited through WeChat and QQ, and the same questionnaire carried the MPATS, which the paper itself describes as a tool 'for measuring mobile phone addiction among Chinese college students'. That is an inference, disclosed. The xlsx was also saved from Chinese-locale Excel (see above). MAPPING (paper_order; Step 5b PARTIAL): the paper gives no item wording but states 'Items 1, 2, 4, 6, and 7 are positively rated and items 3, 5, 8, 9, and 10 are negatively rated, with a total score ranging from 0 to 30' -- which follows the UMD page's own scoring text ('For items 3,5,8,9,10 (which are reversed in valence...)... The scale ranges from 0-30'), so RSESn was aligned to UMD form item n. Checked against the data (verify_song_2023_rses.R, VERDICT: PASS): with stored values the correlation matrix splits into {1,2,4,6,7,8} (within-class mean r 0.571-0.697, cross 0.107-0.267) and {3,5,9,10} (within 0.532-0.662, cross 0.116-0.270); the rival circulated ordering (reverse-worded at 2,5,6,8,9) predicts a {2,5,6,9} cluster and violates for 5 of 10 items (e.g. RSES2 within 0.366 vs cross 0.546). Does NOT establish order within a polarity class (RSES1<->RSES2 or RSES9<->RSES10 swaps are invisible). RESPONSE STORAGE -- ALREADY REVERSE-SCORED: summing the stored columns as they are gives M 29.918 SD 4.788 alpha 0.863 against the published 29.92 / 4.79 / 0.863; un-reversing 3,5,9,10 gives 27.563 / 3.540 / 0.658. The stored MPATS columns reproduce its published 45.96 / 11.91 and r(RSES, MPATS) = -0.336 exactly as Table 2 prints, confirming high stored RSES = high self-esteem. So option_text for RSES3, RSES5, RSES9, RSES10 runs 1=Strongly agree .. 4=Strongly disagree, and for RSES1,2,4,6,7 runs 1=Strongly disagree .. 4=Strongly agree. (The live table is 1-4, not the 0-3 the paper's '0 to 30' implies: the published M 29.92 is only reachable on 10-40.) SOURCE OVERRIDE -- RSES8 DIRECTION: the paper lists item 8 as negatively rated, but its stored values behave as UNREVERSED agreement, and it ships 1=Strongly disagree .. 4=Strongly agree. Evidence: (a) RSES8 clusters with the positive items (r 0.54-0.59 with each) and not with the reversed negatives (r 0.01-0.16); (b) its counts 14/96/798/330 put 91.1% at 3-4 -- under the paper's keying that would be 91.1% of Chinese medical students DISagreeing that they wish they had more respect for themselves, whereas qi_2025_self_esteem (Chinese students, stored raw, paper-stated 1=SD..4=SA) shows 125/134 = 93.3% agreeing with the same item; (c) flipping RSES8 would move the total to 28.586 / 4.230 / alpha 0.793, off every published figure, so the authors themselves summed it as stored. This is the item-8 anomaly recorded for Chinese RSES administrations (see qi_2025_self_esteem). The override is inferential -- the study publishes no anchors -- and is disclosed in public_note. TRANSCRIPTION: item sentences character-for-character from the UMD image (incl. 'I'm'); '**' reverse markers stripped per the page's own instruction ('Do not print the asterisks on the sheet you provide to respondents'); instructions carry only the framing sentence 'BELOW IS A LIST OF STATEMENTS DEALING WITH YOUR GENERAL FEELINGS ABOUT YOURSELF.', verbatim in capitals -- the following SA/A/D/SD circling sentences describe a paper form and were dropped, matching qi_2025_self_esteem. Anchor words are the form's four ('STRONGLY AGREE' .. 'STRONGLY DISAGREE') in sentence case, ordered per item to the stored direction above; the form's own 1=SA..4=SD numbering is not what this table stores. Single trivial section_id; correct_response blank. OCR caution: items were read from a JPEG; spot-check punctuation. RIGHTS: not a block. Register RSES row (verdict ship) applied, not re-derived: 'The Rosenberg Self-Esteem Scale is now in the public domain, meaning you may use it without charge and without notifying the Sociology Department. This permission extends to making translations or adaptations as you see fit...'.
public_note: Respondents were Chinese medical students, but neither the paper nor its data deposit publishes the questionnaire wording (or states its language outright), so IRW ships the Rosenberg Self-Esteem Scale's English original as distributed by the rights holder, with language recorded as Chinese. Responses are stored already reverse-scored, so higher is always higher self-esteem: for RSES3, RSES5, RSES9 and RSES10 a 4 means Strongly disagree. RSES8 ('I wish I could have more respect for myself') is an exception to the paper's own keying: the paper lists it as negatively rated, but its stored values behave as unreversed agreement (91% at 3-4, clustering with the positive items, as is typical of this item in Chinese samples), so it ships with 4 = Strongly agree; the study published no anchors, so this direction is inferred from the data.
